title: Materialize captured phone lists off the launch request
body: Launching a p2p send wrote its ContactInteractionText rows inside the launch request (or the Stripe webhook that finalizes it), reading the captured phone list 1,000 at a time with skip/take. A 200,000-recipient list took 200 reads, each re-sorting and skipping every row before it, plus 200 inserts, all before the response returned. Launch now only locks the filter and enqueues an `outreachMaterialize` message with the outreach id and launch time. The queue handler reads the list by keyset on the recipient id in pages of 10,000 and inserts each page as it arrives (still skipDuplicates, so a redelivery is a no-op), which is 20 of each for the largest list. The loop stops at the audience cap the list was built under instead of an unlimited default, and logs if a capture ever holds more. Sends without a captured list still resolve their filter at launch as before.
author: delegate-eval

 | `outreachInboundSweep.service.ts`                   | Two crons over text/p2p rows with a Peerly job and phone list, already sent, whose send date or last update falls inside a window: `INBOUND_SWEEP_WINDOW_DAYS` (14) for the sweep, `OPT_OUT_RECONCILE_WINDOW_DAYS` (3) for the reconcile. **Hourly sweep** (`outreachInboundSweep`, `30 * * * *` ET, offset from the completion sweep's :00): `PeerlyJobResultsService.fetchInboundCdrRows` streams each job's message report (CDR) through `csv-parser`, drops `sent` rows before validation and enforces a 500MB streamed-byte cap, so a 60MB+ report no longer freezes the 1-vCPU container. Every inbound row is a reply event on `ContactInteractionText`; a row whose Direction is exactly `received` and whose text passes `isOptOutMessage` (`util/textOptOut.util.ts`) is also an opt-out event. Rows with any other Direction are counted (`unexpectedDirectionRows`) and never read for an opt-out. This pass never requests the question-responses report. Cadence decays per Peerly's request-frequency ask (ENG-11038): a job under `INBOUND_SWEEP_FRESH_WINDOW_DAYS` (2) old is swept every pass, an aged one only on hours divisible by `INBOUND_SWEEP_AGED_HOUR_INTERVAL` (6). A per-process `Set<jobId>` skips a job whose previous fetch is still outstanding when the next hour's pass starts. **Opt-out reconcile** (`outreachOptOutReconcile`, `45 * * * *` ET): the backstop for Peerly's own opt-out flags (its AI and texters flag replies that contain no stop word), read from the question-responses report. Peerly builds that report while we wait (up to about 3 minutes for a big job), so each job is read about every `OPT_OUT_RECONCILE_INTERVAL_HOURS` (6, less 30 minutes of slack so a pass starting a moment early in its hour still counts), with one 300s request and `PeerlyHttpService` retries off. Each hourly pass reads `OPT_OUT_RECONCILE_CONCURRENCY` (2) jobs at a time and starts none after `OPT_OUT_RECONCILE_BUDGET_MS` (20 minutes), so it ends long before the next hour's pass; nothing else stops two passes reading the same job at once. `OutreachOptOutReconcile.attemptedAt` records every attempt, a timeout included, so a pass cut short by a deploy or the budget resumes with the never-read jobs first, then the longest-waiting. It lives off the outreach row because a write there bumps `updatedAt`, which holds a send inside the sweep's window. A failure or timeout logs a warn and moves on; the summary counts due, polled, failed, timed-out, deferred (budget spent) and recently read jobs, plus the opt-outs applied, and a pass that ran out of budget also logs a warn. The report's dates carry an offset and are stored as exact instants. Both sources write the same `peerly:<jobId>:<phone>:optout` event id, so either dedupes the other. Both crons claim an hourly `CronLockService` slot (prod runs two replicas, each with its own scheduler) and run only on dev and prod deploys. Returns `{ phonebookPkStr, importedCount }` (local interface — not consumed cross-service). No dialing, no voice-broadcast campaign. **Live-test harness:** when `ROBOCALL_TEST_OVERRIDE_NUMBER` is set, `resolveLandlineNumbers` short-circuits at its top and loads ONLY that one normalized 10-digit number, never resolving the real audience — this method is the single chokepoint for every number that reaches CallHub, so the override guarantees a full real-money flow (hold on the real estimate, dial, capture-actual, refund) can run end to end while no real voter is ever called. Fail-closed: a set-but-malformed value THROWS rather than falling through to the audience (which would dial real people during a test); unset = normal behavior. It does NOT change the pay-step estimate (`deriveBillableCount` resolves the real audience count), so a hold placed for the estimate captures only the one dialed call and refunds the remainder. **Owner phone only:** staging passes `ownerPhoneOnly` for a free robocall offer run (a `GPOFFER-` code) on a demo, test-mode or goodparty.org-owned campaign The schedule-request block's `Scheduled Date` is the candidate's day and wall-clock time in the campaign's zone (`util/scheduledSendLabel.util.ts`: the stored `scheduledLocalDate` + `scheduledLocalTime` when both exist, else the instant, rendered via `resolveSendWindowTimeZone(didState ?? campaign.details.state)` — e.g. `Tue, Oct 6, 2026, 6:00 PM PDT` — comma-separated with no connective word, because the ops-owned Zapier zap that turns this post into a ClickUp task parses this line for the due date), the same values Peerly books and gp-admin shows. Never `String(outreach.date)`: the API runs in UTC, so an evening US send stringified as the NEXT day (CAS read a Tue 6 PM Pacific robocall as "Wed Oct 07", 2026-10-05). The p2p row's `name` carries the same local day (`resolveP2pCreateInputs` formats the payload's calendar day, not the instant). The candidate phone line is the account phone, or `N/A` when the account has none. The interceptor wraps the legacy controller so a failed (possibly paid) send attempt notifies before rethrowing; it sits OUTSIDE `FilesInterceptor` so multipart-parse failures are caught too. Also owns the VO2.0 robocall CAS notices (`notifyRobocallScheduled` posts the same "Campaign Schedule Request" block p2p uses; `notifyRobocallDialing`/`notifyRobocallCompleted` are one-line status updates; `notifyRobocallLowCredit` alerts CAS when a launch is rejected for CallHub `low_credit` so the account can be topped up — fired from the send service's launch-failure path, keyed off `CallhubPermanentError.callhubDetail === CALLHUB_LOW_CREDIT_DETAIL`; `notifyRobocallOverdue` is the one-line "past its scheduled date and still not dialed" page fired by the overdue-alert sweep; `notifyRobocallCanceled` is the one-line "canceled (by staff/candidate)" notice fired from `OutreachRobocallCancelService` so the monitoring team sees cancels like sends) — all best-effort, hung off +  // A redelivery rewrites rows that already exist, which skipDuplicates makes
+  // a no-op, so a fault mid-list throws and the next delivery finishes it.
+  async handleQueuedMaterialization({
+    outreachId,
+    occurredAt,
+  }: OutreachMaterializeMessage): Promise<boolean> {
+    const row = await this.model.findUnique({
+      where: { id: outreachId },
+      include: { campaign: true },
+    })
+    if (!row?.campaign) {
+      this.logger.error(
+        { outreachId },
+        'outreachMaterialize: no such outreach or campaign; acking',
+      )
+      return true
+    }
+    const { campaign, ...outreach } = row
+    await this.materializationService.materializeQueued(
+      campaign,
+      outreach,
+      new Date(occurredAt),
+    )
+    return true
+  }
